Most of the night was spent on the draft recreational marijuana bylaw, with a workshop set for January 22. Minutes were approved and the board went into executive session on litigation.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment on non-agenda items; none.
An Electric Avenue abutter spoke in support of the solar project, preferring it to housing.
A longtime Electric Ave resident preferred solar to a housing development.
Opposed marijuana transporter, research and testing uses and craft home businesses; feared on-site drugs and backlash.
Asked for consistency: marijuana should not get a home-business opportunity other businesses lack.

Approve the site plan waiver for Dix market garden barn

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the two waiver votes, the $100,000 master plan request and the January 22 workshop. They differ on the follow-up items: the solar hearing continuation, the guidebook, the cluster bylaw and the charter question. The thing to know is that our minutes record a "passed" vote to continue the 190 Electric Avenue solar hearing, while the official minutes record no vote and name different hearings for February 11.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the public hearing on the 190 Electric Avenue solar project to February 11 so the applicant can contact neighbors about the reduced vegetative buffer.
The board set a workshop on the draft recreational marijuana bylaw for Tuesday, January 22 at 6:30, after most of the meeting went to the draft.
The board approved a site plan waiver for the Dix market garden barn at 554 Lancaster.
The board accepted a waiver allowing the 119 Mass Ave sign without site plan approval.
The director said a request for funds to update the 2002 master plan would go to the capital planning committee.

why_it_matters: The solar project's buffer and the marijuana bylaw's rules on home businesses and testing uses decide what can be built near homes, and residents may be asked to vote on the bylaw at town meeting.
A master plan update request goes to the capital planning committee, so it would be a spending request that could reach the town budget, mostly taxes.
